title: Writing Files

fakeFiles.story.txt:
Once upon a time.
A robot found a map.
The end.

goal: In this lesson you will learn how to create or overwrite a practice file with mode "w" and write().
learn: Read the file back to check it
idea: To write a file, open it with mode "w", like f = open("diary.txt", "w"). Then use f.write("text\n"). Mode "w" creates the file, or replaces the old contents if it already exists. It is still only the practice folder on this page.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change the second write to "I wrote this myself!\n" and press Run.

practice.text: Write "Hello, file!" plus a newline into hello_out.txt, then read and print it.
practice.hint: f.write() needs a string. Put your message in quotes and add \n at the end so it becomes its own line.
practice.starterTip: Try f.write("Hello, file!\n"). The rest of the starter already reads and prints the file for you.
practice.starter:
f = open("hello_out.txt", "w")
f.write()
f.close()
f = open("hello_out.txt")
print(f.read())
f.close()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if hello_out.txt is written with Hello, file! and then read/printed.

practice.text: Overwrite starter.txt with a new short message, then read and print it.
practice.hint: Mode "w" replaces everything, so pick any short sentence and write it with f.write("your message\n"). The read block below checks it.
practice.starterTip: Example: f.write("My new note!\n"). Run it and the printed text should be your message, not the old starter line.
practice.starter:
f = open("starter.txt", "w")
f.write()
f.close()
f = open("starter.txt")
print(f.read())
f.close()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if starter.txt is overwritten and the new text is printed.

quiz.question: What does mode "w" do if the file already exists?
quiz.correct: Right, "w" wipes the old contents and starts fresh.
quiz.wrong: Write mode starts with an empty file.

quiz.question: Which call puts text into the file?
quiz.correct: Yes, write() puts the string into the file.
quiz.wrong: Use write for output into the file.

quiz.question: Do these writes change your real computer files?

options.text: No. Only the practice folder on the page

quiz.correct: Right, only the practice folder on the page changes.
quiz.wrong: These lessons never touch your real disk.
